<!-- pr-reviewer: 965e09b61edf4d9f9cb33ae515093698af14acf0 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- All 11 replaced `eprintln!` sites keep their message and severity-appropriate level (warn for degraded fallbacks, error for the dead playback thread, caught kernel panic, impossible kind index). Op name became a structured field where the call site has it.
- Nothing is silenced: `camcraft_app::logging::init()` is called first thing in both binaries (`crates/ui/src/main.rs:2` GUI, `crates/app/src/bin/camcraft-cli.rs:5`, which also serves `camcraft-cli mcp` and the bridge). Default filter `info,...` (`crates/app/src/logging.rs`) shows warn and error; writer is `std::io::stderr`, so the MCP JSON-RPC stdout stream is untouched. `CAMCRAFT_LOG` still opens it up.
- `tracing` / `tracing-subscriber` are already direct workspace deps of camcraft-app; the PR touches no Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock, build.rs, scripts or `.github`, so no new dependency decision.
- The ui diag seam (`diag_warn!`, the DIRECT_PRINTS test in `crates/ui/src/diag.rs`) is untouched; the PR changes only camcraft-app.
- New pinning test `a_budget_refusal_names_the_limit_that_fired_at_warn`; decision file `docs/decisions/163-tracing-rest.md` present; no CHANGELOG/snapshot/golden/process-file changes.

**Local results (merged with upstream/main, already up to date)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test logging` | 4 passed |
| top_stock, drill_prior, stock_view, step_chord_units, mcp, carried_verify, rotary_verify | 8, 12, 13, 9, 3, 4, 4 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The full quick-gate app and ui suites were not re-run here (the diff is messages only and ui is untouched); the author reports them green.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `crates/app/src/mcp/bridge.rs:31` lost its `camcraft-cli:` prefix; the tracing target (`camcraft_app::mcp::bridge`) now carries the origin, fine.
- `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs` is far over 400 lines (pre-existing; this PR does not grow it).
- Not exercised by the author or me: a live GUI / MCP session confirming the lines appear on stderr.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 720bd65ebfb27fcb853ec55bbde697bbfd3cf03a -->
Independent review (second pair of eyes after the author's own), on the head that includes the merge with main and PR #911.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

What looks good
- No new dependency: `tracing` and `tracing-subscriber` are already in `crates/app/Cargo.toml` (lines 27-28) and no `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock` change in the diff.
- All 12 replaced `eprintln!` calls keep their message text; only the "camcraft: " prefix goes, since the event target now carries it. Levels are sensible: degraded-but-continuing fallbacks are `warn!`, and the playback-thread death, the caught truck-kernel panic (`step.rs:126`) and the impossible op-kind index are `error!`. Nothing that refuses or loses data dropped below the default `info` filter (`logging::DEFAULT_FILTER`).
- A subscriber is installed: `logging::init()` is called from `crates/ui/src/main.rs:2` (GUI) and `crates/app/src/bin/camcraft-cli.rs:5` (CLI and MCP server). It writes to stderr, so MCP stdout JSON-RPC is untouched. The diagnostics go somewhere.
- The merge with main kept #911: `step.rs` still calls `step_refine::refine` and still logs the reduced-fidelity line, now as `tracing::warn!`.
- New test `a_budget_refusal_names_the_limit_that_fired_at_warn` pins the refusal's level and the limit name.

Local results (merged with main a6bd69d8, trial merge clean)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 114 passed, 0 failed.
- `--test import`: 23 passed; `--test step_chord_units`: 3 passed; `--test model_fidelity`: 9 passed; `--test logging`: 4 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Notes (non-blocking)
- The follow-up for the other crates' ~25 library `eprintln!` calls is recorded as still owed in `docs/decisions/163-tracing-rest.md`; this PR rightly uses `Refs #163`, not `Fixes`.
- Messages with an op name use a structured `op` field; with the default fmt layer the field prints after the message, which reads fine.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
